tasks.title: Initialize Next.js 15 Frontend with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, and shadcn/ui
tasks.description: Set up the frontend project foundation using Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript 5, Tailwind CSS v4 with CSS variables for theming, and shadcn/ui component library. Configure the development environment with proper tooling.
tasks.details:
1. Create Next.js 15 app with App Router:
   ```bash
   npx create-next-app@latest frontend --typescript --tailwind --eslint --app --src-dir --import-alias "@/*"
   ```

2. Install and configure Tailwind CSS v4 (currently v4.0.x):
   - Update tailwind.config.ts with CSS variable-based theming
   - Configure content paths for components and pages
   - Set up dark mode with 'class' strategy for next-themes compatibility

3. Initialize shadcn/ui (latest v2.x):
   ```bash
   npx shadcn@latest init
   ```
   - Select 'new-york' style for modern look
   - Configure CSS variables for theming
   - Install core components: button, input, textarea, card, dialog, dropdown-menu, tooltip, scroll-area, avatar, badge, separator

4. Install additional dependencies:
   ```bash
   npm install next-themes zustand react-markdown remark-gfm rehype-highlight highlight.js lucide-react
   ```

5. Configure TypeScript paths in tsconfig.json for clean imports

6. Create base directory structure:
   ```
   frontend/src/
   ├── app/
   │   ├── layout.tsx
   │   ├── page.tsx
   │   ├── globals.css
   │   ├── (auth)/
   │   ├── chat/
   │   ├── skills/
   │   └── documents/
   ├── components/
   │   ├── ui/           # shadcn components
   │   ├── chat/
   │   ├── skills/
   │   ├── layout/
   │   └── theme/
   ├── hooks/
   ├── lib/
   │   ├── supabase/
   │   ├── api.ts
   │   └── utils.ts
   ├── stores/
   └── types/
   ```

7. Configure globals.css with CSS variables for light/dark themes:
   ```css
   :root {
     --background: 0 0% 100%;
     --foreground: 222.2 84% 4.9%;
     /* ... other semantic color variables */
   }
   .dark {
     --background: 222.2 84% 4.9%;
     --foreground: 210 40% 98%;
     /* ... dark theme overrides */
   }
   ```

8. Create root layout.tsx with basic HTML structure and font loading (Inter or Geist)
tasks.testStrategy:
1. Run `npm run dev` and verify dev server starts on localhost:3000 without errors
2. Verify TypeScript compilation succeeds with `npm run build`
3. Check Tailwind CSS is generating styles by adding test classes
4. Verify shadcn/ui components render correctly by importing a Button
5. Confirm directory structure matches specification
6. Run ESLint with `npm run lint` and ensure no errors

subtasks.title: Create Next.js 15 App with create-next-app and Basic Configuration
subtasks.description: Initialize the Next.js 15 project using create-next-app with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, ESLint, App Router, and src directory structure. Verify the initial setup works correctly.
subtasks.details:
Run the create-next-app command to scaffold the project:
```bash
npx create-next-app@latest frontend --typescript --tailwind --eslint --app --src-dir --import-alias "@/*"
```

This will create a Next.js 15 project with:
- TypeScript configuration with tsconfig.json
- Tailwind CSS pre-configured (v3.x by default, will be upgraded in subtask 2)
- ESLint with Next.js rules
- App Router structure in src/app/
- Path alias @/* configured for clean imports

After creation, navigate into the frontend directory and verify the development server starts correctly. Check that the default page renders at localhost:3000.

1. Run `cd frontend && npm run dev` and verify server starts on localhost:3000
2. Open browser to http://localhost:3000 and confirm Next.js default page renders
3. Run `npm run build` to verify TypeScript compilation succeeds
4. Check tsconfig.json contains the @/* path alias configuration
5. Verify src/app/layout.tsx and src/app/page.tsx exist

subtasks.title: Initialize shadcn/ui and Install Core Components
subtasks.description: Set up shadcn/ui component library with the new-york style, configure it to use CSS variables, and install the core UI components needed for the chat application.
subtasks.details:
Initialize shadcn/ui and install required components:

1. Run shadcn/ui init:
```bash
npx shadcn@latest init
```
When prompted:
- Style: new-york
- Base color: Slate (or Neutral)
- CSS variables: Yes
- React Server Components: Yes
- Components directory: src/components/ui

2. This creates components.json with configuration

3. Install core components:
```bash
npx shadcn@latest add button input textarea card dialog dropdown-menu tooltip scroll-area avatar badge separator
```

4. Install additional dependencies for the chat app:
```bash
npm install next-themes zustand react-markdown remark-gfm rehype-highlight highlight.js lucide-react
```

5. Verify components.json is properly configured:
```json
{
  "$schema": "https://ui.shadcn.com/schema.json",
  "style": "new-york",
  "rsc": true,
  "tsx": true,
  "tailwind": {
    "config": "tailwind.config.ts",
    "css": "src/app/globals.css",
    "baseColor": "slate",
    "cssVariables": true
  },
  "aliases": {
    "components": "@/components",
    "utils": "@/lib/utils"
  }
}
```
subtasks.testStrategy:
1. Verify components.json exists with correct configuration
2. Check src/components/ui/ directory contains all installed components
3. Verify lib/utils.ts was created with cn() utility function
4. Import and render a Button component in page.tsx to verify it works
5. Run `npm run build` to verify all components compile correctly
6. Test that lucide-react icons render correctly


- src/lib/utils.ts (should exist from shadcn)

```json
{

    "baseUrl": ".",
```

tasks.title: Initialize FastAPI Backend with Project Structure and Core Configuration
tasks.description: Set up the Python FastAPI backend with proper project structure, dependency management using pyproject.toml, configuration handling, CORS setup, and health check endpoint.
tasks.details:
1. Create backend directory and initialize Python project:
   ```bash
   mkdir -p backend/app
   cd backend
   python -m venv .venv
   source .venv/bin/activate
   ```

2. Create pyproject.toml with dependencies (Python 3.12+):
   ```toml
   [project]
   name = "chat-app-backend"
   version = "0.1.0"
   requires-python = ">=3.12"
   dependencies = [
       "fastapi>=0.115.0",
       "uvicorn[standard]>=0.32.0",
       "python-dotenv>=1.0.0",
       "pydantic>=2.10.0",
       "pydantic-settings>=2.6.0",
       "supabase>=2.11.0",
       "anthropic>=0.42.0",
       "sse-starlette>=2.2.0",
       "python-multipart>=0.0.18",
   ]
   [project.optional-dependencies]
   dev = ["pytest>=8.0", "pytest-asyncio>=0.24.0", "httpx>=0.28.0"]
   ```

3. Create app/config.py with Pydantic Settings:
   ```python
   from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings
   
   class Settings(BaseSettings):
       supabase_url: str
       supabase_anon_key: str
       supabase_service_role_key: str
       anthropic_api_key: str
       cors_origins: list[str] = ["http://localhost:3000"]
       debug: bool = False
       
       class Config:
           env_file = ".env"
   ```

4. Create app/main.py with FastAPI app:
   ```python
   from fastapi import FastAPI
   from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
   from app.config import Settings
   
   settings = Settings()
   app = FastAPI(title="Chat App API", version="0.1.0")
   
   app.add_middleware(
       CORSMiddleware,
       allow_origins=settings.cors_origins,
       allow_credentials=True,
       allow_methods=["*"],
       allow_headers=["*"],
   )
   
   @app.get("/health")
   async def health_check():
       return {"status": "healthy"}
   ```

5. Create directory structure:
   ```
   backend/
   ├── app/
   │   ├── __init__.py
   │   ├── main.py
   │   ├── config.py
   │   ├── auth/
   │   │   └── __init__.py
   │   ├── routers/
   │   │   └── __init__.py
   │   ├── services/
   │   │   └── __init__.py
   │   ├── tools/
   │   │   └── __init__.py
   │   ├── models/
   │   │   └── __init__.py
   │   ├── utils/
   │   │   └── __init__.py
   │   └── db/
   │       └── __init__.py
   ├── tests/
   │   └── __init__.py
   ├── .env.example
   ├── pyproject.toml
   └── Dockerfile
   ```

6. Create .env.example with all required environment variables

7. Create Dockerfile for production deployment:
   ```dockerfile
   FROM python:3.12-slim
   WORKDIR /app
   COPY pyproject.toml .
   RUN pip install .
   COPY app/ ./app/
   CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
   ```
tasks.testStrategy:
1. Install dependencies with `pip install -e .` and verify no errors
2. Run `uvicorn app.main:app --reload` and confirm server starts on localhost:8000
3. Test health endpoint: `curl http://localhost:8000/health` returns {"status": "healthy"}
4. Verify CORS headers present in response for allowed origins
5. Test environment variable loading by checking settings object
6. Run pytest to ensure test infrastructure works

subtasks.title: Implement Pydantic Settings Configuration Module
subtasks.description: Create the app/config.py module using Pydantic Settings for type-safe environment variable configuration with validation and sensible defaults.
subtasks.details: Create backend/app/config.py using pydantic_settings.BaseSettings class. Define Settings class with the following fields: supabase_url (str), supabase_anon_key (str), supabase_service_role_key (str), anthropic_api_key (str), cors_origins (list[str] with default ['http://localhost:3000']), debug (bool with default False). Configure the class to read from .env file using model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file='.env', env_file_encoding='utf-8'). tasks.title: Create Supabase Database Schema with Migrations and RLS Policies
tasks.description: Design and implement the complete database schema for threads, messages, skills, skill_files, code_executions, and sandbox_files tables with proper indexes, foreign keys, and Row Level Security policies.
tasks.details:
1. Initialize Supabase local development:
   ```bash
   npx supabase init
   npx supabase start
   ```

2. Create migration file: supabase/migrations/001_initial_schema.sql

3. Create threads table:
   ```sql
   CREATE TABLE threads (
       id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
       user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
       title TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'New Chat',
       created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
       updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
   );
   CREATE INDEX idx_threads_user_id ON threads(user_id);
   CREATE INDEX idx_threads_updated_at ON threads(updated_at DESC);
   ```

4. Create messages table:
   ```sql
   CREATE TABLE messages (
       id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
       thread_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES threads(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
       user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
       role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('user', 'assistant', 'system')),
       content TEXT NOT NULL,
       tool_calls JSONB DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
       created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
   );
   CREATE INDEX idx_messages_thread_id ON messages(thread_id);
   CREATE INDEX idx_messages_created_at ON messages(created_at);
   ```

5. Create skills table:
   ```sql
   CREATE TABLE skills (
       id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
       user_id UUID REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
       name VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
       description VARCHAR(1024) NOT NULL CHECK (char_length(description) >= 20),
       instructions TEXT NOT NULL,
       enabled BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
       license VARCHAR(64),
       compatibility VARCHAR(64),
       metadata JSONB DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
       created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
       updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
       CONSTRAINT skills_name_format CHECK (name ~ '^[a-z0-9-]+$')
   );
   CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_skills_user_name ON skills(COALESCE(user_id, '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'), name);
   ```

6. Create skill_files table:
   ```sql
   CREATE TABLE skill_files (
       id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
       skill_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES skills(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
       user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
       filename TEXT NOT NULL,
       file_size BIGINT NOT NULL,
       mime_type TEXT NOT NULL,
       storage_path TEXT NOT NULL,
       created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
   );
   CREATE INDEX idx_skill_files_skill_id ON skill_files(skill_id);
   ```

7. Create code_executions table:
   ```sql
   CREATE TABLE code_executions (
       id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
       thread_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES threads(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
       user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
       code TEXT NOT NULL,
       stdout TEXT,
       stderr TEXT,
       exit_code INTEGER,
       status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running' CHECK (status IN ('running', 'completed', 'failed')),
       execution_time_ms INTEGER,
       created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
   );
   ```

8. Create sandbox_files table:
   ```sql
   CREATE TABLE sandbox_files (
       id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
       execution_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES code_executions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
       user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
       filename TEXT NOT NULL,
       file_size BIGINT NOT NULL,
       mime_type TEXT NOT NULL,
       storage_path TEXT NOT NULL,
       created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
   );
   ```

9. Create RLS policies:
   ```sql
   ALTER TABLE threads ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
   CREATE POLICY threads_select ON threads FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
   CREATE POLICY threads_insert ON threads FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);
   CREATE POLICY threads_update ON threads FOR UPDATE USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
   CREATE POLICY threads_delete ON threads FOR DELETE USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
   
   -- Similar policies for all other tables
   -- Skills: user_id = auth.uid() OR user_id IS NULL (for global skills)
   ```

10. Create updated_at trigger function and apply to relevant tables

11. Create Supabase Storage buckets: skill-files, sandbox-outputs
tasks.testStrategy:
1. Run `npx supabase db reset` and verify migration applies cleanly
2. Test RLS by attempting to access another user's data (should fail)
3. Test all CRUD operations on each table via Supabase client
4. Verify foreign key constraints by attempting to create orphan records
5. Test unique constraints (skill name per user)
6. Verify indexes are created with `\d+ table_name` in psql
7. Test storage bucket creation and access policies

subtasks.title: Initialize Supabase Local Development and Create Migration File Structure

Verify config.toml settings match project requirements (project_id, ports, auth settings). The migration file has been created at supabase/migrations/20240101000000_initial_schema.sql. SELECT current_database(), current_user, version();
```sql
-- Check auth.users table exists
SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = 'auth' AND table_name = 'users');
```

subtasks.title: Create and Verify Threads and Messages Tables with Indexes
subtasks.description: Implement and verify the threads and messages tables with proper UUID primary keys, foreign key references to auth.users, check constraints for message roles, JSONB tool_calls field, and appropriate indexes for query performance.

Test inserting a thread and message to verify constraints work. Test CASCADE delete by deleting a user and confirming threads/messages are removed.

subtasks.title: Create and Verify Skills and Skill Files Tables with Unique Constraints
subtasks.description: Implement and verify the skills table with nullable user_id for global skills, kebab-case name validation regex, description length check, and composite unique index. Create skill_files table with file metadata and storage path reference.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify skills table accepts valid kebab-case names and rejects invalid ones (uppercase, special chars, starting with number). Test unique constraint prevents duplicate names for same user_id and for global skills. Test description minimum length check (20 chars). Verify skill_files FK cascade works when skill is deleted.

subtasks.title: Create and Verify Code Executions and Sandbox Files Tables
subtasks.description: Implement and verify the code_executions table for tracking sandbox code execution results with status enum, exit codes, and timing. Create sandbox_files table for storing file outputs from code execution.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test code_executions status constraint accepts only 'running', 'completed', 'failed'. Verify CASCADE delete from thread removes code_executions and sandbox_files. Test inserting execution with all fields and verify nullable fields accept NULL. Test sandbox_files CASCADE delete when execution is removed.

subtasks.title: Implement and Verify Comprehensive RLS Policies for All Tables

tasks.title: Build Chat Backend with LLM Integration and SSE Streaming
tasks.description: Implement the chat API endpoint with Server-Sent Events streaming, integrate Anthropic Claude as the primary LLM, and create the thread and message management backend services.
tasks.details:
1. Create LLM service (backend/app/services/llm.py):
   ```python
   from anthropic import Anthropic
   from typing import AsyncIterator
   
   class LLMService:
       def __init__(self, api_key: str):
           self.client = Anthropic(api_key=api_key)
       
       async def stream_completion(
           self,
           messages: list[dict],
           system: str,
           model: str = "claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
           tools: list[dict] | None = None,
       ) -> AsyncIterator[dict]:
           with self.client.messages.stream(
               model=model,
               max_tokens=4096,
               system=system,
               messages=messages,
               tools=tools,
           ) as stream:
               for event in stream:
                   yield self._format_event(event)
   ```

2. Create message models (backend/app/models/chat.py):
   ```python
   from pydantic import BaseModel
   
   class MessageCreate(BaseModel):
       content: str
       thread_id: str | None = None
   
   class Message(BaseModel):
       id: str
       thread_id: str
       role: str
       content: str
       tool_calls: list[dict] = []
       created_at: datetime
   ```

3. Create thread service (backend/app/services/threads.py):

   ```python
       async def create_thread(self, user_id: str, title: str = "New Chat") -> dict
       async def get_threads(self, user_id: str) -> list[dict]

       async def update_thread(self, thread_id: str, user_id: str, title: str) -> dict
       async def delete_thread(self, thread_id: str, user_id: str) -> bool
       async def get_messages(self, thread_id: str, user_id: str) -> list[dict]
   ```

4. Create chat router (backend/app/routers/chat.py):
   ```python
   from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends
   from sse_starlette.sse import EventSourceResponse
   
   router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/chat", tags=["chat"])
   
   @router.post("/")
   async def chat(
       request: MessageCreate,
       user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
   ):
       async def event_generator():
           # Create/get thread
           # Save user message
           # Load conversation history
           # Stream LLM response
           # Save assistant message
           for event in llm_service.stream_completion(...):
               yield {"event": event["type"], "data": json.dumps(event["data"])}
       
       return EventSourceResponse(event_generator())
   ```

5. Create threads router (backend/app/routers/threads.py):
   ```python
   @router.get("/")
   async def list_threads(user: User = Depends(get_current_user)):
       return await thread_service.get_threads(user.id)
   
   @router.post("/")
   async def create_thread(user: User = Depends(get_current_user)):
       return await thread_service.create_thread(user.id)
   
   @router.patch("/{thread_id}")
   async def update_thread(thread_id: str, title: str, user: User = Depends(get_current_user)):
       return await thread_service.update_thread(thread_id, user.id, title)
   
   @router.delete("/{thread_id}")

       return await thread_service.delete_thread(thread_id, user.id)
   ```

6. Register routers in main.py:

tasks.title: Build Docker Sandbox Manager for Secure Python Code Execution
tasks.description: Create the Docker-based sandbox system for executing Python code securely, including custom Docker image with pre-installed packages, container lifecycle management with TTL, and security restrictions.
tasks.details:
1. Create custom Docker image (docker/sandbox/Dockerfile):
   ```dockerfile
   FROM python:3.12-slim
   
   # Install common data science packages
   RUN pip install --no-cache-dir \
       numpy==2.1.0 \
       pandas==2.2.3 \
       matplotlib==3.9.2 \
       seaborn==0.13.2 \
       scikit-learn==1.5.2 \
       scipy==1.14.1 \
       pillow==10.4.0 \
       requests==2.32.3 \
       beautifulsoup4==4.12.3 \
       openpyxl==3.1.5 \
       ipython==8.28.0
   
   # Create sandbox user (non-root)
   RUN useradd -m -s /bin/bash sandbox
   
   # Create output directory
   RUN mkdir -p /sandbox/output && chown sandbox:sandbox /sandbox/output
   
   # Set working directory
   WORKDIR /sandbox
   USER sandbox
   
   # Security: no network access will be enforced at runtime
   ```

2. Build and tag image:
   ```bash
   docker build -t chat-app-sandbox:latest docker/sandbox/
   ```

3. Create sandbox manager service (backend/app/services/sandbox.py):
   ```python
   import docker
   import asyncio
   from datetime import datetime, timedelta
   
   class SandboxManager:
       def __init__(self):
           self.client = docker.from_env()
           self.sessions: dict[str, SandboxSession] = {}
           self.default_ttl = timedelta(minutes=30)
       
       async def get_or_create_session(self, thread_id: str, user_id: str) -> SandboxSession:
           key = f"{user_id}:{thread_id}"
           if key in self.sessions:
               session = self.sessions[key]
               session.refresh_ttl()
               return session
           
           container = self.client.containers.run(
               "chat-app-sandbox:latest",
               detach=True,
               stdin_open=True,
               tty=True,
               network_disabled=True,  # No network access
               mem_limit="512m",       # Memory limit
               cpu_period=100000,
               cpu_quota=50000,         # 50% CPU
               pids_limit=100,          # Process limit
               read_only=False,         # Allow writes to /sandbox/output
               volumes={
                   f"/tmp/sandbox-{key}": {"bind": "/sandbox/output", "mode": "rw"}
               }
           )
           
           session = SandboxSession(container, thread_id, user_id)
           self.sessions[key] = session
           return session
       
       async def execute_code(
           self,
           session: SandboxSession,
           code: str,
           timeout: int = 60
       ) -> AsyncIterator[ExecutionEvent]:
           # Execute code in IPython kernel
           # Stream stdout/stderr
           # Handle timeout
           # Collect generated files
           pass
       
       async def cleanup_expired_sessions(self):
           # Called periodically to remove expired containers
           pass
   
   class SandboxSession:
       def __init__(self, container, thread_id: str, user_id: str):
           self.container = container
           self.thread_id = thread_id
           self.user_id = user_id
           self.expires_at = datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(minutes=30)
           self.variables = {}  # Track Python variables
       
       def refresh_ttl(self):
           self.expires_at = datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(minutes=30)
   ```

4. Create execution events:
   ```python
   class ExecutionEvent:
       START = "start"
       STDOUT = "stdout"
       STDERR = "stderr"
       FILE = "file"
       COMPLETE = "complete"
       ERROR = "error"
       TIMEOUT = "timeout"
   ```

5. Create security policy:
   ```python
   BLOCKED_PATTERNS = [
       r"import\s+os",
       r"import\s+subprocess",
       r"import\s+socket",
       r"open\s*\([^)]*['\"]/(etc|proc|sys)",
       r"__import__",
       r"eval\s*\(",
       r"exec\s*\(",
   ]
   
   def validate_code(code: str) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
       for pattern in BLOCKED_PATTERNS:
           if re.search(pattern, code):
               return False, f"Blocked: {pattern}"
       return True, None
   ```

6. Create background cleanup task:
   ```python
   @app.on_event("startup")
   async def start_cleanup_task():
       asyncio.create_task(periodic_cleanup())
   
   async def periodic_cleanup():
       while True:
           await sandbox_manager.cleanup_expired_sessions()
           await asyncio.sleep(60)  # Check every minute
   ```

7. Create docker-compose.yml for development:
   ```yaml

       build:
         context: ./docker/sandbox

       image: chat-app-sandbox:latest
   ```

tasks.title: Implement Persistent Tool Memory with Result Storage and History Reconstruction
tasks.description: Build the tool result persistence system to store tool call results in the message JSONB column and reconstruct proper tool call message sequences when loading conversation history for the LLM.
tasks.details:
1. Update message model to handle tool calls (backend/app/models/chat.py):
   ```python
   class ToolCall(BaseModel):
       id: str
       name: str
       input: dict
       result: str | None = None  # Populated after execution
   
   class Message(BaseModel):
       id: str
       thread_id: str
       role: str  # 'user', 'assistant', 'tool_result'
       content: str
       tool_calls: list[ToolCall] = []
       created_at: datetime
   ```

2. Create tool memory service (backend/app/services/tool_memory.py):
   ```python
   MAX_RESULT_SIZE = 50_000  # 50KB limit per result
   
   class ToolMemoryService:
       async def store_tool_result(
           self,
           message_id: str,
           tool_call_id: str,
           result: str
       ) -> None:
           # Cap result size
           if len(result) > MAX_RESULT_SIZE:
               result = result[:MAX_RESULT_SIZE] + "\n... [truncated]"
           
           # Update message's tool_calls JSONB
           await self.db.execute(
               """
               UPDATE messages
               SET tool_calls = jsonb_set(
                   tool_calls,
                   '{$index,result}',
                   $result::jsonb
               )
               WHERE id = $message_id
               """,
               {"message_id": message_id, "tool_call_id": tool_call_id, "result": result}
           )
       
       async def reconstruct_history(
           self,
           thread_id: str,
           user_id: str
       ) -> list[dict]:
           """Reconstruct messages for LLM context with tool call/result pairs."""
           messages = await self.db.fetch_all(
               "SELECT * FROM messages WHERE thread_id = $1 ORDER BY created_at",
               [thread_id]
           )
           
           llm_messages = []
           for msg in messages:
               if msg['role'] == 'user':
                   llm_messages.append({
                       "role": "user",
                       "content": msg['content']
                   })
               elif msg['role'] == 'assistant':
                   # Check for tool calls
                   tool_calls = msg.get('tool_calls', [])
                   if tool_calls:
                       # Assistant message with tool_use blocks
                       content = []
                       if msg['content']:
                           content.append({"type": "text", "text": msg['content']})
                       for tc in tool_calls:
                           content.append({
                               "type": "tool_use",
                               "id": tc['id'],
                               "name": tc['name'],
                               "input": tc['input']
                           })
                       llm_messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": content})
                       
                       # Tool result messages
                       for tc in tool_calls:
                           if tc.get('result'):
                               llm_messages.append({
                                   "role": "user",
                                   "content": [{
                                       "type": "tool_result",
                                       "tool_use_id": tc['id'],
                                       "content": tc['result']
                                   }]
                               })
                   else:
                       llm_messages.append({
                           "role": "assistant",
                           "content": msg['content']
                       })
           
           return llm_messages
   ```

3. Update chat flow to use tool memory:
   ```python
   # In chat router
   async def chat_handler(...):
       # Load history with tool results
       history = await tool_memory_service.reconstruct_history(thread_id, user_id)
       
       # Stream response
       assistant_message = None
       async for event in llm_service.stream_completion(history, system_prompt, tools):
           if event['type'] == 'message_start':
               # Create assistant message record
               assistant_message = await create_message(
                   thread_id, user_id, 'assistant', '', []
               )
           elif event['type'] == 'tool_use':
               # Record tool call in message
               await add_tool_call(assistant_message['id'], event['tool'])
               
               # Execute tool
               result = await execute_tool(event['tool']['name'], event['tool']['input'])
               
               # Store result
               await tool_memory_service.store_tool_result(
                   assistant_message['id'],
                   event['tool']['id'],
                   result
               )
               
               # Send result back to LLM
               yield {"event": "tool_result", "data": result}
   ```

4. Add result size capping:
   ```python
   def cap_result(result: str, max_size: int = MAX_RESULT_SIZE) -> str:
       if len(result) <= max_size:
           return result
       
       # Try to preserve structure (for JSON)
       if result.strip().startswith('{') or result.strip().startswith('['):
           try:
               data = json.loads(result)
               # Truncate at object level
               truncated = truncate_json(data, max_size)
               return json.dumps(truncated) + "\n... [truncated]"
           except:
               pass
       
       return result[:max_size] + "\n... [truncated]"
   ```
